title: SofaBuffers Generator Config Schema
description: Validates sofabgen configuration files (YAML or JSON). PLAN §7. Every level is closed (additionalProperties:false) so typos are rejected, not ignored. Every key in this schema is honored by the generator; the schema and the set of consumed keys are kept in lockstep.

max_dyn_array_count.description: Receiver-side decode limit: maximum element count accepted for an UNBOUNDED array (one without a schema `count`). Exceeding it fails the decode with the corelib's LimitExceeded error - never a clamp. Unset (the default) = unlimited (today's behavior). Fields with a schema `count` are governed by that bound instead (generator#100); a field that legitimately needs more than this cap gets an explicit schema bound. Not honored by targets whose storage is statically schema-bounded (c, cpp corelib: c-cpp, rust no_std).

max_dyn_string_len.description: Receiver-side decode limit: maximum byte length accepted for an UNBOUNDED string (one without a schema `maxlen`). Checked at the length header, before the payload is buffered or allocated; exceeding it fails the decode with the corelib's LimitExceeded error. Unset (the default) = unlimited. Fields with a schema `maxlen` are governed by that bound instead. Not honored by statically bounded targets (c, cpp corelib: c-cpp, rust no_std).

max_dyn_blob_len.description: Receiver-side decode limit: maximum byte length accepted for an UNBOUNDED blob (one without a schema `maxlen`). Checked at the length header, before the payload is buffered or allocated; exceeding it fails the decode with the corelib's LimitExceeded error. Unset (the default) = unlimited. Fields with a schema `maxlen` are governed by that bound instead. Not honored by statically bounded targets (c, cpp corelib: c-cpp, rust no_std).

emit.description: sources (default): just the message-type source files. project: additionally scaffold a buildable project (build files + the canonical-JSON conformance harness).

namespace.description: Namespace wrapping the generated types, for the targets that have one (C++ namespace, C# namespace). No generic default on purpose: each backend applies its own idiomatic default (C++ `message`, C# `Message`).

input_dir.description: Directory of message definitions to generate from. The CLI --in flag overrides it.

output_dir.description: Directory the generated files are written to. The CLI --out flag overrides it.

tool_banner.description: Tool name stamped into every generated file header (default: sofabgen).

license.description: SPDX license identifier stamped into every generated file header (e.g. MIT, Apache-2.0, LicenseRef-Acme). Unset or `none` (the default) emits no SPDX line.

symbol_prefix.description: Prefix applied to every generated C symbol - struct typedefs, descriptor tables, and the encode/decode/init functions (default: message_).

allow_dynamic.description: Storage for schema-bounded fields. false = heap-free inline containers (sofab::FixedString<N> / FixedBytes<N> / InlineVector<T,N>); true = std::string / std::vector, sized to what a message actually carries. The wire is identical either way -- this is a storage decision, never a format or API one. DEFAULT DEPENDS ON corelib: false for c-cpp (an embedded target has no heap to spare), true for cpp (a server target would rather allocate what it carries than its declared worst case). Unbounded fields differ by profile, not by this switch: c-cpp rejects them at generate time in both modes (maxlen/count are mandatory), while cpp simply leaves them in their dynamic container -- so static storage can be turned on there without changing the schema, and applies per field wherever a bound exists. A declared bound is honoured whatever its size; there is no threshold above which it silently falls back to the heap.

corelib.description: Which C++ corelib the generated code targets. cpp (default): pure-C++20 header-only corelib-cpp with dynamic containers (std::vector/std::string). c-cpp: the C++ wrapper over corelib-c-cpp with fixed-capacity, heap-free containers sized from the schema.

namespace.description: C++ namespace wrapping the generated types (default: message). Overrides generic.namespace for this target.

allow_dynamic.description: Storage for schema-bounded fields. true = String / Vec, holding what a message actually carries; false = fixed-capacity heapless::String<N> / heapless::Vec<T, N> sized from the schema bound. The wire is identical either way -- this is a storage decision, never a format or API one. DEFAULT DEPENDS ON corelib: false for rs-no-std (a firmware target has no heap to spare), true for rs (a server target would rather allocate what it carries than its declared worst case). Unbounded fields differ by profile, not by this switch: rs-no-std rejects them at generate time in both modes (maxlen/count are mandatory), while rs simply leaves them in String/Vec -- so static storage can be turned on there without changing the schema, and applies per field wherever a bound exists. Selecting it on rs adds a heapless dependency to the generated crate. The Rust analog of the C++ allow_dynamic.

corelib.description: Which Rust corelib the generated crate targets. rs (default): the std corelib-rs, tuned for throughput. rs-no-std: the #![no_std] corelib-rs-no-std, feature-gated per wire type and tuned for footprint.

no_std.description: rust corelib: rs-no-std only. Emit a genuinely #![no_std], heap-free crate: heapless::String<N>/Vec<T,N> fixed-capacity fields sized from the schema, a bounded decode stack, and serde gated behind a cargo feature. On by default for corelib: rs-no-std; set false to emit an ordinary std crate against the no-std corelib.

package.description: The `package <name>` clause of the generated .go files (default: message).

module_path.description: The module path written to the generated go.mod in project mode (default: example.com/generated).

go_version.description: The `go <version>` directive written to the generated go.mod in project mode (default: 1.21).

package.description: The `package <name>;` declaration of the generated classes, and the Maven source-directory layout in project mode (default: message).
The `package <name>` declaration of the generated Kotlin files, and the source-directory layout in project mode (default: message).

namespace.description: The `namespace <name>` wrapping the generated classes (default: Message). Overrides generic.namespace for this target.

int64.description: 64-bit field representation. bigint (default): bigint scalars and bigint[] arrays. long: u64[]/i64[] backed by corelib Long[] behind a get/set accessor pair (bigint-free encode/decode hot path; assignment accepts Long | bigint | number); scalars stay bigint. number: additionally maps u64/i64 scalars to number - the caller guarantees scalar values fit the +/-2^53 safe-integer range. All modes are wire-identical.

format.description: Documentation output format. html (default, and currently the only format): a single self-contained page (inline CSS, no external assets) documenting every message and named type.

max_message_size.description: Ceiling on a message's encoded size, in bytes. Serves two roles. (1) FALLBACK: a message with an unbounded field (an array without `count`, a string/blob without `maxlen`) has no computable worst case; the generated code then emits this value as MAX_SIZE_LIMIT and aliases MAX_SIZE to it, so the number is visibly imposed rather than derived. (2) BUDGET: when set explicitly it is also checked - a schema whose computed worst case exceeds it fails generation, which is where a message that cannot fit the target transport should be caught. A message the schema DOES bound keeps its exact computed size; this key never replaces a number the schema can supply. Unset = 4096.
